> Overall, 146 (49.2%) participants were classified as SOCI-0, 94 (31.6%) as SOCI-1, 37 (12.5%) as SOCI-2, and 20 (6.7%) as SOCI-3.

> These findings provide biomarker support for Jak/Bondi actuarial MCI criteria, complementing evidence of improved diagnostic precision, stronger AD biomarker associations, fewer false positives, and better identification of individuals at risk of progression. 46, 47 Importantly, all participants had global CDR=0 and were classified as CU after extensive evaluation by dementia specialists.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

report: Reporting *p* values imprecisely (e.g., *p* < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in *p* value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., *p* = .032) unless *p* values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use *p* < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., "decreased at the *p* < .05 significance threshold").

```{r}
#| echo: false


# table data --------------------------------------
table <- structure(list("P-Value" = c("p<0.05", "p>0.05", "p<0.05", "p<0.05", 
"p<0.05", "p<0.05"), Text = c("SOCI stages were modelled as a four-level categorical variable, with SOCI-0 as the reference and statistical significance defined at FDR p<0.05.", 
"The groups did not differ in age, sex, education, or CL values (all p>0.05).", 
"MoCA scores differed across groups (p=0.0002); compared with SOCI-0 participants, scores were lower in the SOCI-2 and SOCI-3 groups, and the SOCI-3 group had lower scores than the SOCI-1 group (Holm-adjusted p<0.05).", 
"Tukey-adjusted comparisons showed greater tau burden in SOCI-3 than all other stages across all [¹ F]MK6240 measures and both [¹ F]flortaucipir SEOT measures (all p<0.05).", 
"For each significant measure, SOCI-3 had greater tau burden than all other stages in Tukey-adjusted comparisons (all p<0.05).", 
"Maps display voxels surviving FDR correction (p<0.05).")), row.names = c(NA, 
-6L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"))

# display table -----------------------------------
metacheck::report_table(table, c(0.1, 0.9), 2, FALSE)
```

live_data_statements: Participants were assigned hierarchically to four mutually exclusive SOCI stages based on abnormal scores within and across domains (Figure 1B).
Written informed consent was obtained from all participants.
Overall, 146 (49.2%) participants were classified as SOCI-0, 94 (31.6%) as SOCI-1, 37 (12.5%) as SOCI-2, and 20 (6.7%) as SOCI-3.

These findings provide biomarker support for Jak/Bondi actuarial MCI criteria, complementing evidence of improved diagnostic precision, stronger AD biomarker associations, fewer false positives, and better identification of individuals at risk of progression. 46, 47 Importantly, all participants had global CDR=0 and were classified as CU after extensive evaluation by dementia specialists.

text.text: Background and Objectives: Tau-PET is associated with subtle objective cognitive impairment (SOCI) in clinically unimpaired (CU) individuals, but whether the spatial patterns and strengths of these associations differ across tracers remains unclear.
We performed a head-to-head comparison of [¹ F]MK6240 and [¹ F]flortaucipir to investigate their associations with SOCI in CU individuals.
We cross-sectionally assessed CU participants from the HEAD study who underwent both tau-PET scans.

Linear regressions examined associations between domain-specific cognition and tau burden using standardized uptake value ratios (SUVR) in regional and voxelwise analyses, alongside regional spatial extent of tauopathy (SEOT) measures.
Tau burden was compared across groups representing different levels of SOCI.
Models adjusted for age, sex, and education, with additional adjustment for amyloid-β burden.
Centiloid-stratified analyses examined associations across amyloid-β burden levels.
Results: Among 297 participants (mean [SD] age, 67.0 [8.4] years; 179 [60.3%] female), higher [¹ F]MK6240 SUVR was associated with poorer memory performance.
Greater SEOT with either tracer was associated with poorer memory and showed nominal associations with executive dysfunction.
Regional association strengths did not differ significantly between tracers, while SEOT yielded comparable or stronger associations than SUVR.
Centiloid-stratified analyses revealed taucognition associations primarily at intermediate and high amyloid-β burden.
[¹ F]MK6240 showed more spatially extensive voxelwise associations with memory and across SOCI group comparisons.
Regional analyses also yielded more statistically significant differences across SOCI groups with [¹ F]MK6240 than with.

In the revised Alzheimer's Association research and diagnostic framework, "clinical stage 2 -transitional decline" is recognized as a phase of Alzheimer's disease (AD), encompassing subtle cognitive or behavioral changes with minimal impact on daily functioning. 1 Among these manifestations are objectively detectable cognitive changes that do not meet criteria for mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia, a phenotype broadly referred to in the literature as subtle objective cognitive impairment (SOCI). 2 SOCI is identified through standardized neuropsychological assessment and may occur with or without subjective cognitive complaints. 2 However, the specific criteria used to operationalize SOCI vary widely and include performance on individual tests or composite scores, longitudinal intra-individual decline, clinical ratings, and data-driven approaches. 2 Although these definitions converge on the detection of subtle cognitive changes before conventional MCI criteria are met, associations between SOCI and AD biomarkers have varied. [3] [4] [5] [6] This variability may reflect not only differences in SOCI definitions but also differences in the sensitivity of biomarkers and measurement approaches.

text.text: Among currently available biomarkers of core AD pathologies, tau positron emission tomography (tau-PET) is most closely associated with cognitive symptoms. 7 In clinically unimpaired (CU) individuals, greater tau-PET uptake has been associated with poorer performance across several cognitive domains. [8] [9] [10] [11] Understanding these early associations has become increasingly relevant as tau-PET is incorporated as an endpoint in preventive trials. 12 In this context, tracer differences in sensitivity could influence the correspondence between tau-PET and clinical outcomes, affecting the interpretation and comparability of biomarker findings across trials.

text.text: Therefore, we compared the FDA-approved [¹ F]Flortaucipir and [¹ F]MK6240 head-to-head regarding their associations with subtle cognitive differences in preclinical AD.
Specifically, we aimed to clarify how tau-PET tracer choice influences the characterization of the earliest measurable cognitive manifestations of AD.
Secondarily, we investigated whether tau spatial extent provides information beyond conventional SUVR measures in capturing the tau-PET correlates of SOCI.

In this cross-sectional study, we assessed individuals diagnosed as CU from the HEAD study (https://head-study.info/), recruited across eight sites in the United States and Canada between November 2022 and March 2025.

text.text: Participants underwent structural MRI, tau-PET imaging with both [¹ F]Flortaucipir and [¹ F]MK6240, and amyloid-β (Aβ) PET imaging (either [¹¹C]PiB, [¹ F]AZD4694, or [¹ F]Florbetaben, depending on site preference).

HEAD imaging protocols have been described previously. 13 Briefly, MRI was acquired on 3T scanners using ADNI-4-aligned protocols, 18 including high-resolution sagittal T1-weighted images obtained with three-dimensional accelerated MPRAGE or IRSPGR sequences.

text.text: PET acquisition windows after intravenous bolus injection were 40-60 or 50-70 min for [¹¹C]PiB, 90-110 min for [¹ F]florbetaben, 50-70 min for [¹ F]AZD4694, 90-110 min for [¹ F]MK6240, and 80-100 min for [¹ F]flortaucipir.

PET images were reconstructed into four 5-min frames using scanner-specific ordered-subset expectation maximization-based algorithms with standardized parameters and no smoothing, with corrections for attenuation, motion, dead time, radioactive decay, scatter, and random events.

Images were processed using a validated PET-MRI pipeline. 13 T1-weighted MRI was nonlinearly registered to the ICBM 2020 Nonlinear Symmetric template using Advanced Normalization Tools (ANTs). 19 PET images were linearly coregistered to native-space T1-weighted MRI, then warped into ICBM 2020 stereotaxic space using the concatenated PET-to-T1 and T1-to-template transformations.

text.text: T1-derived whole-brain masks excluded extracerebral voxels, and scanner-specific Gaussian smoothing yielded a uniform 8-mm full width at half maximum.

text.text: Statistical analyses were conducted in R version 4.4.1.
ROI-based associations between tau-PET SUVR and cognitive performance were evaluated using separate linear regression models for each cognitive domain, tracer, and ROI (MTL and neocortex).
Cognitive scores and tau-PET measures were z-standardized using the full study sample.
Models were adjusted for age, sex, and education, with additional models further adjusted for CL.
In secondary analyses, those models were repeated using tau-PET SEOT in place of SUVR as the main predictor.

False discovery rate (FDR) correction was performed using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure separately for each tau-PET metric-cognitive outcome pair, with each family comprising four tests (2 tau-PET tracers × 2 ROIs).
Sensitivity analyses were conducted using the entorhinal as the ROI.
Effect-size differences were evaluated using 5,000 paired participant-level bootstrap resamples of 297 participants sampled with replacement.

Models used identical resampled participants, outcomes, and covariates; standardized coefficients were recalculated to obtain paired tracer ([¹ F]MK6240 minus [¹ F]flortaucipir) and metric (SEOT minus SUVR) differences.
We further explored SUVR-cognition associations within CL-defined subgroups using linear regressions adjusting only for demographic covariates.
FDR correction was applied separately for each tau-PET ROI-cognitive domain pair across the three CL groups and two tau-PET tracers, yielding six tests per correction family.

Voxel-based linear regression analyses were performed in R (RMINC package), with tau-PET as the dependent variable and cognitive measures as the independent variables, adjusting for age, sex, and education.
Secondary models further adjusted for CL.
Statistical significance was determined using an FDR p<0.05.

text.text: This cross-sectional, head-to-head study examined associations of [¹ F]flortaucipir and [¹ F]MK6240 measures with subtle objective cognitive deficits in CU individuals.
Both tracers showed modest cognitive associations, but [¹ F]MK6240 demonstrated more spatially extensive tau-SOCI associations and more frequent significant differences in uptake between SOCI stages.
SEOT complemented SUVR through additional and stronger cognitive associations and more frequent significant differences between SOCI stages.

These findings extend evidence that tau-PET captures subtle cognitive variation early in AD, potentially informing participant characterisation and outcome assessment in preventive trials. 12 Our results align with cross-sectional evidence linking greater tau-PET burden to poorer cognitive performance in CU individuals.

text.text: Its proximity to the meninges and skull warrants caution because extracerebral spill-in may explain the association rather than cortical tau. 36, 37 Taken together, our findings reinforce the broader tau-PET literature by showing convergent associations between tau-PET uptake and subtle, domain-specific cognitive performance across two tracers, while also revealing potentially tracer-specific association patterns.

text.text: Beyond tracer-related differences, tau-cognition associations also varied across the preclinical AD continuum.
No significant associations emerged in CL LOW , suggesting that associations at higher Aβ levels may preferentially reflect AD-related tau pathology.
Consistent with this interpretation, MTL tau-PET signal in Aβ-CU individuals has been associated with age but not age-adjusted objective cognition.
Tau-cognition associations involved both MTL and neocortical ROIs in CL INT but only neocortical tau in CL HIGH .
Although none survived FDR correction, this pattern suggests that regional tau correlates of SOCI may differ by Aβ burden.

Neocortical associations in CL INT and CL HIGH may reflect Aβ-associated tau spread beyond the MTL, consistent with longitudinal evidence that antecedent Aβ accumulation predicts subsequent tau accumulation, which relates to cognitive decline in CU individuals. 10 Beyond supporting AD progression models, these findings may inform preventive trials stratifying CU participants by Aβ burden, such as AHEAD 3-45. 12 Although grouping strategies may differ across trials, our results suggest that regional tau-PET correlates of subtle cognitive variation may vary across Aβ-defined populations.

text.text: Nevertheless, no subgroup associations survived FDR correction, so these findings remain hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger longitudinal samples.
Although both tracers captured SOCI, only [¹ F]MK6240 showed significant SUVR-based ROI associations with cognitive composites.
It also showed broader voxelwise associations with memory, often affected early in typical AD, 39 and more extensive voxelwise and regional uptake differences across SOCI groups.

text.text: These findings align with [¹ F]MK6240's greater affinity and sensitivity for tau neurofibrillary tangles (NFT) 40 and head-to-head evidence suggesting earlier detection of biologically meaningful tau burden than [¹ F]flortaucipir. 13 Neuropathological reports also indicate limited [¹ F]flortaucipir sensitivity to low-density MTL tau, particularly without advanced Aβ pathology. 41 These characteristics may explain broader [¹ F]MK6240 associations with subtle clinical variation here and with other transitional decline features, including mild behavioral impairment. 42 Despite more frequent significant associations with [¹ F]MK6240, between-tracer ROI effect-size differences did not survive FDR correction.

text.text: Restricted tau and cognitive ranges in this CU sample may have limited detection of these differences.

Broader [¹ F]MK6240 associations therefore do not establish superior clinical performance; implications for individual-level detection, prognosis, and clinical decisions remain uncertain in preclinical AD.
Longitudinal studies must determine whether these cross-sectional differences confer meaningful advantages in detecting and predicting the earliest cognitive manifestations of tau pathology.
Beyond tracer comparisons, we examined whether tau-PET metrics influenced SOCI associations within tracers.
Both metrics captured cognitive associations, with SEOT performing at least comparably to SUVR and identifying additional significant associations in selected analyses.

Notably, higher neocortical SEOT in participants with mildly impaired MoCA scores accords with evidence that MoCA declines as tau extends into the neocortex, 43 suggesting that SEOT may capture the earliest cognitively detectable phase of this spread.

text.text: Supporting this interpretation, extent-based measures capture greater interindividual variability at low tau levels and may better reflect early regional tau propagation in AD. 14 Although SEOT advantages were not consistent across cognitive outcomes, selected associations were stronger and no formal comparison favoured SUVR.

text.text: Adding SEOT may therefore modestly improve sensitivity to early cognitive differences.

This aligns with evidence that tau extent and load differ in their associations with downstream cognitive and neurodegenerative changes, providing potentially complementary information across the AD continuum. 15, 44 Selective advantages may reflect the limited tau burden and cognitive variation expected in CU individuals.

text.text: Greater tau-PET burden in those meeting actuarial MCI criteria therefore suggests that these criteria may detect biologically meaningful cognitive changes before clinically apparent impairment.
By contrast, SOCI-2 participants (Edmonds/Thomas-like actuarial obj-SCD) did not differ in tau-PET burden from SOCI-0 or SOCI-1.

text.text: Nevertheless, longitudinal measures do not necessarily yield stronger associations with tau pathology. 49 In a neuropathological study of individuals who remained CU near death, Braak NFT stage alone was not associated with antemortem longitudinal trajectories in episodic memory, executive function, or global cognition. 50 Thus, longitudinal ascertainment may therefore improve SOCI construct validity without ensuring direct correspondence with tau burden.

text.text: These findings highlight the need to compare heterogeneous SOCI definitions 2 for biomarker and prognostic validity.

Extending criteria to broader batteries and validating alternative neuropsychological measures may clarify which psychometric definitions best characterize SOCI within Alzheimer's Association clinical stage 2. 1 Study strengths include a unique, substantial sample of well-characterized CU individuals imaged with two widely used tau-PET tracers.

text.text: However, without goldstandard neuropathological evaluation, we cannot directly establish which tracer more accurately reflects biologically relevant NFT pathology.
The multicenter design reduces single-site dependence, but exclusively North American recruitment warrants replication in more diverse populations and settings to establish generalizability.
Another limitation is the cross-sectional operationalization of the SOCI.

Because longitudinal data from the HEAD cohort are not yet extensively available, we could not incorporate intra-individual longitudinal cognitive change, as adopted in other work 49 and in the Alzheimer's Association workgroup framework. 1 Moreover, although SOCI criteria were adapted from validated approaches, [29] [30] [31] battery differences prevented exact implementation and may have influenced classification and biomarker associations.
